name: Web - Table Tap
description: Table Tap is a web application allowing customers to order directly at their table in a bar/restaurant. Orders are then sent to the kitchen, where staff can validate and serve them. The admin side allows management of available menu products and access to sales statistics on the dashboard. This project was completed by a team of 3 people in 7 weeks.

skill.skill: Development of a complete CRUD system (Create, Read, Update, Delete)
skill.example: I designed and implemented a management system allowing users to create, view, modify, and delete products, categories, and promo codes. This system is based on clear and modular logic, facilitating the addition of new entities as needed.

skill.skill: Use of reactive programming with RxJS (BehaviorSubject)
skill.example: To improve user experience, I implemented a real-time preview of products being created or modified. This feature allows instant visualization of entered data, such as name, price, category, or associated icons.

The interface includes informative icons to indicate whether a product is vegetarian, gluten-free, or spicy, helping users quickly understand product characteristics. A dynamic search bar also allows easy retrieval of products from the database.
Forms handle complex data structures (categories, subcategories, multiple options) while remaining intuitive and user-friendly.

skill.skill: Creation of a promo code management module
skill.example: I developed an interface for adding custom promotional codes with a name and discount percentage. These elements are also subject to CRUD operations, allowing complete management through the application.
To give the project a visual identity, I designed the application logo myself, in harmony with the overall interface atmosphere.

name: Web - Shake it!
description: 'Shake it!' is a cocktail creation game made in 2 days. Using ingredients, players can create cocktails of their choice. Once all ingredients are gathered in the shaker, just Shake it! and the cocktail is ready.

skill.skill: Implementation of an interactive drag & drop system
skill.example: Ingredients are added to the shaker via a drag-and-drop mechanism, offering a playful and intuitive user experience. This allows visual cocktail composition directly in the interface.

skill.skill: Development of a complete CRUD system for cocktails
skill.example: Users can create new cocktails, view existing ones, modify them (name, ingredients, etc.), or delete them. This system ensures flexible and personalized recipe management.

skill.skill: Custom logo creation for the application
skill.example: I created the application logo to bring a coherent and professional visual identity to the interface.

name: Unity - Pachinko Game
description: A Pachinko game where the goal is to drop a ball in the right place to score the most points.

skill.example: I used simple objects (spheres, cubes, etc.) to create a functional game foundation, facilitating gameplay testing before potential graphic iterations.

skill.skill: Implementation of a drag & drop system for ball control
skill.example: Players can move the ball horizontally via a drag-and-drop mechanism, allowing dynamic targeting of the target box.

skill.skill: Addition of audio and visual elements to enrich the experience
skill.example: Background music accompanies the player throughout the game, and sound effects as well as visual effects were added to mark important actions and enhance immersion.

name: Mod - Path to Menzoberranzan
description: Path to Menzoberranzan is a Baldur's Gate 3 campaign mod offering an entirely new adventure independent from the base game. It features iconic zones from Baldur's Gate 2, taking place in the regions of Athkatla and Menzoberranzan. Players will enjoy an immersive experience with brand new gameplay, fully voice-acted companions, and a rich story. The project is still in development.

skill.example: After only a few months on the project, I was promoted to Technical Gameplay Lead. I now oversee the implementation of gameplay, mechanics, and player-oriented systems. I notably designed the gameplay portion of the technical skill check used to recruit new programmers.

skill.skill: Programming and scripting in Divinity Engine 4
skill.example: I wrote complex scripts to manage the quest system (flags, triggers, conditions) as well as debug scripts. I also implemented branching dialogues influenced by companions present in the party or player choices.
I integrated interactive objects such as books containing custom text, and configured companions via complete root templates (stats, behaviors, etc.).
I generated basic timelines to accompany dialogues with appropriate cinematics, significantly improving staging, interaction fluidity, and narrative immersion.
I participated in pull request reviews, with a continuous QA approach to ensure mod stability and consistency.

I created a complex dialogue example that was used as a reference and learning tool for new team members. I also helped write internal documentation to standardize programming and integration best practices and facilitate team onboarding.

As the programming team representative in an interdisciplinary team, I ensure mediation between teams, conflict management, internal moderation, and member tracking (staff records, disciplinary actions, etc.).

This project allowed me to learn to collaborate with a dozen programmers within a structured pipeline (180 people across all teams), adopt a more rigorous workflow, and better integrate the constraints of a large-scale community project.

name: Unity - UI Flow
description: This project consists of implementing a complete menu system for a video game, including management of main player options. It covers essential features such as volume control, fullscreen mode, preference saving, and navigation between different game scenes. The goal was to design a solid, reusable, and easily extensible foundation for future projects.

skill.skill: Creation of a functional options menu
skill.example: I designed and implemented an options menu allowing players to modify game settings in real-time, with a clear and accessible interface.
Implementation of sliders to adjust volume (music and SFX), with immediate application of changes in-game.
Addition of a system allowing activation or deactivation of fullscreen mode from the options menu.
Player-chosen settings (volume, fullscreen) are saved and automatically restored at game launch through the use of PlayerPrefs.
Implementation of navigation logic between different game scenes (main menu, game, return to menu), ensuring smooth and consistent transitions between game states.

skill.skill: Scene transitions with fade in / fade out
skill.example: Implementation of a visual transition system between scenes to improve readability and user comfort during game state changes.

name: Unity - Arcade pickup game
description: This project is a small 2D Unity prototype highlighting UI management, gameplay, and audio systems. The player collects pickups while staying in the play area, with score, timer, and highscore persistence.

skill.example: Implementation of a smooth control system using Player Input.
Random pickup generation via a PickupSpawner, with spawn zone verification to prevent objects from leaving the screen.
Creation of a score system that increments upon pickup collection, allowing player progress tracking.
Addition of a timer limiting game duration and a Game Over panel with options to restart the game.
Implementation of a persistent highscore system using PlayerPrefs, to save and display the best score between game sessions.

name: Unity - Nova, a bartending game (prototype)
description: Nova is a narrative visual novel developed in Unity, where the player takes on the role of a bartender serving cocktails to clients with unique personalities. The game blends branching narrative (via Ink) with interactive mixology gameplay, featuring a recipe discovery system and relationship progression.

skill.example: I designed all game visuals: characters, backgrounds, UI, and interface elements, creating a cohesive visual identity centered around the night bar atmosphere.
I wrote the entire scenario and dialogues using the Ink language, creating three characters with distinct personalities and designing a branching narrative system with relationship progression.

I structured the project with reusable and extensible systems. The game's grimoire uses a generic system capable of displaying both character profiles and cocktail recipes, making it easy to add new content without rewriting code.

I used an existing Ink wrapper and developed the narrative flow logic, including the pause/resume dialogue system during transitions to the mixology mini-game and back to the main scene, ensuring smooth narrative continuity.

I created a data manager that saves player progression (characters met, recipes discovered) in memory only for a smooth prototype experience. The system automatically notifies the interface of new discoveries through an event system.

I developed a drag & drop system allowing players to drag ingredients into a shaker, with dynamic reparenting to display elements above the entire interface. The game verifies if the combination matches an existing recipe, properly handling duplicate ingredients.

I designed multiple screens: a double-page grimoire with navigation, a dialogue history with character-based coloring, mouse-following tooltips, and an end-of-day screen progressively revealing cards of encountered characters. I added smooth animations (glass shaking, bounce effect appearance, fade transitions).

I implemented a system dynamically loading and unloading scenes (bar, main scene, card screen) while maintaining game state. The system automatically detects where the player comes from to resume dialogue at the correct point.

I integrated an audio manager with music playlist (shuffle/loop), interface sounds, and sound effects synchronized with animations. I used coroutines to detect track endings without continuous checking, optimizing performance.

I added an arcade mode allowing players to enjoy only the mixology mini-game without narrative progression, with automatic game mode detection and interface adaptation (Reset button instead of Serve, skipping the discovery system).

I performed thorough cleanup of the entire project (30+ scripts): removing debug logs, adding comprehensive documentation, code optimization, and safeguarding against common errors. I particularly focused on readability and maintainability to facilitate future development.
I diagnosed and fixed several complex issues related to scene loading timing, code duplication, and protecting internal data against accidental modifications.

This project allowed me to master advanced Unity aspects: event systems for component decoupling, Canvas and RectTransform manipulation for UI, coroutines for animations, GameObject lifecycle, and architecture with generic interfaces.

name: Unity - Ghost Tamagotchi
description: Ghost Tamagotchi is a Unity 2D game where the player takes care of a little ghost with needs to manage and a narrative evolution system. The game combines real-time stat management with evolution choices that influence the ghost's appearance across three life stages: baby, teen, and adult.

skill.example: I structured the project around a C# Actions system to fully decouple components. GhostStats doesn't know about the UI, GhostUI doesn't know about the SpriteManager - each system subscribes to the events it needs with no direct dependencies, eliminating memory leak risks.

I designed a three-stage progression system with evolution pop-ups offering four player choices, including a random option. Each choice influences the ghost's final sprite. The system pauses stat decay during choices and stops cleanly once the adult stage is reached.

I implemented a dynamic color system on the stat bars (green / orange / red based on thresholds) and conditional end states: game over if a stat reaches zero, or a happy ending if the ghost reaches adulthood.
I built a centralized audio manager handling looping background music and sound effects.

I added a back-and-forth animation to the ghost with automatic horizontal flip and random pauses to bring the character to life, along with a visible countdown before each evolution to keep the player engaged.
I configured the Canvas Scaler to adapt the UI to different resolutions and deployed the game as a WebGL build on Unity Play.
